name: seed_benchmark
description: NEEDS TWO PATH SUBSTITUTIONS BEFORE IT WILL RUN -- see _model_paths below. How much of the agent's win rate is the training seed? Six models, each as the pure-network agent against SakkirinaSolo over the same 400 games: the five per-seed models from scripts/slurm_train.sh, plus the shipped model as a sixth point on the same seed_base so it sits in the same distribution rather than beside it.
_first_run_was_invalid: THE FIRST RUN OF THIS CONFIG IS INVALID. Its results are being kept under
experiment_results/calibration/, so someone will find them and they look fine. They are not.
Job 4457064, 2400 games, all completed cleanly. The five seed rows produced win rates of
78.5, 75.5, 79.5, 78.0 and 68.0 percent -- an entirely plausible spread.
WHY THEY ARE INVALID. Each seed model carried 14,000-19,000 subnormal weights, an artefact
of training on x86 rather than on Apple Silicon, which flushes denormals in hardware.
Subnormal arithmetic falls off onnxruntime's fast path, so the seed models ran at a median
640-790 us per inference against the shipped model's ~58 us, and completed roughly
1,350-1,510 evaluations per turn against the shipped row's 6,401. They were searching about
a QUARTER as much as the model they were being compared against, in an experiment whose
entire premise is that the six models differ only in training seed.
NOTHING FAILED. Every game finished. No timeouts, no disqualifications, no errors, and win
rates that looked like ordinary seed variance. The only visible symptom anywhere was the
evaluations-per-turn column -- which exists only because equal_effort needed it, and which
nothing would have prompted anyone to read on a config about training seeds. Had the column
not been there, this would have gone into the paper.
THE FIX. The five models were re-exported with denormal flushing (training/export_to_onnx.py
zeroes |w| < 1e-30 by default). They now run at 44-50 us, and tools/compare_onnx_models.py
confirms zero output difference across 2000 real states per seed -- same models, same
predictions, ~15x faster. allowed_onnx_sha256 and the per-matchup notes above carry the
re-exported hashes; the old ones are superseded and must not be re-added.
THE SHIPPED ROW WAS UNAFFECTED. Tasks 2000-2399 ran the shipped model, which has no
subnormal weights, at 6,401 evaluations per turn. Those results are valid and were kept.
_check_before_interpreting: BEFORE INTERPRETING THE RERUN, CHECK THE EVALUATIONS-PER-TURN COLUMN.
Every seed row's mean evaluations per turn should land near the shipped row's ~6,400. If a
seed row comes back at ~1,400 instead, that row did NOT run the re-exported model -- most
likely SOT_MODEL_PATH still points at a pre-flush .onnx, or a stale copy was left in place.
This check is not optional and it is not a formality. The first run failed in exactly this
way and produced clean, plausible, completely wrong numbers; the win rates alone will not
tell you which run you are looking at. The hash pin in allowed_onnx_sha256 now rejects the
old files outright, so a repeat should abort rather than mislead -- but verify the column
anyway, because the pin is a set check and cannot tell one allowed model from another.
_model_paths: EVERY SOT_MODEL_PATH BELOW MUST BE EDITED BEFORE SUBMITTING. Two substitutions:
CHANGE_ME_HPCWORK   -> the literal expansion of $HPCWORK on your cluster
(echo $HPCWORK on the login node), e.g. /hpcwork/yfl79180
CHANGE_ME_REPO_ROOT -> the absolute path of this checkout,
e.g. /home/you/tot/deepsets-tales-of-tribute
THE PATHS MUST BE ABSOLUTE. Not a style preference -- a relative path is
resolved against two DIFFERENT working directories on the way to the bot:
- tools/benchmark_cluster.py checks os.path.isfile(SOT_MODEL_PATH) from
wherever the harness was invoked;
- the game runs with cwd=GameRunner/bin/Release/net8.0, and the bot calls
File.Exists on the same string from THERE.
So a relative path can satisfy the harness and still miss in the bot -- and a
miss in the bot is SILENT: DeepSetsBotExp logs the rejection and falls back to
its normal resolution, which finds GameRunner's own copy of the shipped model.
Every seed row would then quietly benchmark the shipped model instead.
$HPCWORK IS NOT EXPANDED. Nothing between this file and the bot runs a shell:
the env dict is passed verbatim into the child process, so a literal
"$HPCWORK/..." stays a literal dollar sign and the file is simply not found.
Substitute the expanded path by hand.
An unedited config cannot run by accident: tools/benchmark_cluster.py checks
that SOT_MODEL_PATH exists BEFORE launching the game and aborts the task with
exit 1 and no result file if it does not. CHANGE_ME_* paths fail that check.
_what_the_pin_does_and_does_not_guarante: allowed_onnx_sha256 lists all six hashes because the pin is checked per task
against whatever that task's SOT_MODEL_PATH names. That is a SET check, so it
guarantees 'this task loaded one of our six known models' -- it does NOT
guarantee 'seed 3's row loaded seed 3's model'. The harness has one allowed
list per config, not one per matchup.
For most configs that distinction is irrelevant; here it is the whole point of
the experiment, so check identity separately before submitting:
and compare against the table in REPRODUCE.md section 3. Every result JSON also
records its task's full env, so which path each matchup actually used is
_comparability: WHY THE SHIPPED MODEL IS A MATCHUP HERE AND NOT A NUMBER COPIED IN.
The shipped model's 79.3% against SakkirinaSolo came from alpha_sweep.json at
alpha0=0. That config has seed_base 20260922; this one has 20260928. Different
seed base means different games -- different deals, different opponents' draws,
a different sample. Dropping 79.3% into a table beside these five would be
comparing one model on one set of 400 games against five models on a different
set of 400 games, and the difference between the two sets is not zero.
So the shipped model gets its own matchup in THIS config, on THIS seed_base,
playing the same 400 games as the seeds. Six models, one set of games,
like-for-like. The alpha_sweep figure stays where it is and is not reused here.
Note the seeds' games are still not PAIRED with each other: seed = seed_base +
task_id and task ids run contiguously across matchups, so each matchup plays a
different 400 games. They are six independent samples from one population, not
six readings of one set of positions. Read differences against the Wilson
intervals the aggregator prints, not as a ranking.

matchups.note: The shipped model, on the same seed_base as the five seeds so it is a sixth point in the same distribution -- see _comparability. Its val loss is not in this table on purpose: 0.4034 was measured on a DIFFERENT validation set from the seeds' and is not comparable to theirs. Set explicitly rather than left unset so the plan and every result JSON record which model this row used; leaving it unset would resolve to GameRunner's own copy, which is the same file but says so nowhere. Last in the config, so it can be dropped by simply not submitting its task-id range without renumbering any seed row.
